task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle; no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The browser fingerprint value is carried through runtime-derived transport keys and recovered shortly before console output.
The collect route selects its live configuration only after click-time browser capability signals are collected.

The click path crosses delegated event handling, action routing, gate checks, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, runtime slot materialization, fingerprint encoding, dynamic transport and sink wrapping.
The same collect interaction emits non-target shadow objects carrying browser_fp-like values before the target fingerprint.collect object.
The deployed bundle also contains decoy reducers that execute or remain reachable-looking without feeding the target browser_fp field.
The target value is separated from the click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame, MutationObserver and DOM CustomEvent boundaries.
The selected runtime configuration is cloned and mutated in a WeakMap-backed materialization step before the encoder receives it.
The final sink receives an already encoded value after dynamic cell and lane recovery, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.reason: The observable value is a stable compact encoding of browser capability signals (userAgent, screen dimensions, devicePixelRatio, hardwareConcurrency, colorDepth, timezone offset). It is not a request signature, state code, byte-array transform or request-body rewrite.

near_categories.why_not: The chain uses browser capability collection, not UI form state as the target behavior.
The output has no proof/token/seal semantics tied to a request; fingerprint-like decoy code in the bundle does not feed the target field.
No network request body is emitted or rewritten; the target is a console-observable fingerprint value.
